guitar.notes: Manu Chao plays varied guitars, no single iconic documented model.

tone.target: dirty punk-funk crunch with slight fuzz edge
tone.profile: dirty punk-funk crunch with slight fuzz edge
tone.summary: A gritty, mid-focused punk-funk tone achieved using a fuzz/OD boost into a British dirty amp model, paired with a tight 4x12 cabinet.

rig.name: Mano Negra - King Kong Five - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up high-gain noise and hum inherent in punk/funk recording.
Provide the initial gritty overdrive and mid-punch required for punk funk.
blocks.gap: The 'Green OD' is used to simulate a dirty, aggressive boost rather than a polite clean tone.

blocks.purpose: Add the required 'fuzz edge' and raw, aggressive grit to push the tone into punk territory.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is chosen for its mid-focused aggression, fitting the dirty punk aesthetic better than a Muff or Distortion.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a dirty British combo amp (Marshall/dirty combo clue) with strong mid-range punch.
Provide the tight, aggressive sound and classic British cabinet tone suggested by the genre.
Sculpt the tone to maximize mid-punch and ensure a tight, focused attack.
blocks.gap: Using EQ 2 allows for more aggressive shaping of the mids compared to EQ 1.

blocks.purpose: Keep the signal path clean and focused on raw aggression; no wah needed for this punk funk style.
Keep modulation off to maintain the dry, aggressive, and raw punk sound.
Add minimal, natural ambience to prevent the tone from sounding too sterile or overly compressed.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly (low mix) to maintain dryness while adding depth.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for a more aggressive, raw punk/funk edge.

proposals.recommendedAsset: dirty 4x12 or vintage British cab IR
proposals.reason: Enhance the rawness and grit needed for dirty punk-funk.
